label: Area
title: Area
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Volume and magnitude over an ordered domain, with filled series from `@chartkitdev/core`.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Volume and magnitude over an ordered domain, with filled series from `@chartkitdev/core`.
anatomy: 1Axes — ordered domain on X, quantitative scale on Y. Labels and ticks come from the theme unless you override.
2Filled series — area under the curve from `series[].data`. Curve, stack, and fill opacity live on the mark; fill is always on for area.
3Tooltip — hover read of domain + value. Agents rarely need to configure this for a first render.

label: Line
title: Line
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Trends over an ordered domain, rendered from `@chartkitdev/core`.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Trends over an ordered domain, rendered from `@chartkitdev/core`.
anatomy: 1Axes — ordered domain on X, quantitative scale on Y. Labels and ticks come from the theme unless you override.
2Series — one or more lines from `series[].data`. Curve, markers, and optional area fill live on the mark.
3Tooltip — hover read of domain + value. Agents rarely need to configure this for a first render.

label: Bar
title: Bar
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Categories and magnitudes as bars from `@chartkitdev/core`. Vertical or horizontal; stack or group with `encoding.series`.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Categories and magnitudes as bars from `@chartkitdev/core`. Vertical or horizontal; stack or group with `encoding.series`.
anatomy: 1Axes — category band on X (or Y when `mark.orientation` is `horizontal`), quantitative scale on the other. Tick labels come from the theme unless you override.
2Bars — one mark per category (or per series × category). `mark.gap`, `mark.cornerRadius`, `mark.stack`, and `mark.fillOpacity` shape the fill.
3Tooltip — hover read of category + value (and series when stacked/grouped). Agents rarely need to configure this for a first render.

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: phase-3 `bar-range` / `errorbar` (those are `extra`), `interact`, or Mermaid. Stacked example with horizontal bars: `examples/03-bar-stacked.json` (`mark.stack: "stack"`, `mark.orientation: "horizontal"`).
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { bar } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/bar"; export const render = createRenderer([bar]); // Adapters default to core/all — pass `render` to stay minimal. // Measured bar path: 34,373 B gzip (chartkit-minimal, measured-sizes.json).`

label: Donut
title: Donut
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Part-to-whole slices with a hole from `@chartkitdev/core`. Use `type: "pie"` for a solid disk (`innerRadius` defaults to 0); donut defaults to `0.6`.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Part-to-whole slices with a hole from `@chartkitdev/core`. Use `type: "pie"` for a solid disk (`innerRadius` defaults to 0);

options.role: Gap between slices in degrees (donut default 2)
Pull named slices out from centre

anatomy: 1Slices — one arc per category from `encoding.x` / `encoding.y`. `mark.sort`, `mark.other`, and `mark.padAngle` control order, small-slice folding, and gaps.
2Hole — `mark.innerRadius` (donut default `0.6`). Set `0` or use `type: "pie"` for a solid pie. Optional center KPI is common in product UIs (mock-plausible in the try rail).
3Labels / tooltip — `mark.labels` with leader lines outside; hover still works via `interact`. Agents rarely need tooltip config for a first render.

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: `interact` (attach for hover/selection), phase-3 extras, or Mermaid. For a solid pie prefer `type: "pie"` rather than forcing `innerRadius: 0` on donut — both are valid; pie’s defaults (`innerRadius` 0, `padAngle` 0) match the solid-disk look.
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { donut } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/donut"; export const render = createRenderer([donut]); // Pie: import { pie } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/pie"; // Measured donut path: 14,266 B gzip (chartkit-minimal, measured-sizes.json).`

label: Combo
title: Combo
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Mixed marks on a shared X axis from `@chartkitdev/core`. Put each series’ mark on `encoding.y[].mark` (`bar`, `line`, `area`, or `range`) and send a secondary scale to `axis: "y2"`.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Mixed marks on a shared X axis from `@chartkitdev/core`. Put each series’ mark on `encoding.y[].mark` (`bar`, `line`, `area`,

options.role: Range band fields when mark is range
Bar band gap on combo bars

anatomy: 1Shared X — one categorical/temporal domain for every series. Bars, lines, areas, and range bands all align on the same band scale.
2Layered marks — per-series `encoding.y[].mark`: `bar`, `line`, `area`, or `range` (lo/hi band under other series). Global `mark.*` (points, stack, gap) still apply where the schema says “combo”.
3y2 — set `axis: "y2"` on a channel and configure `axes.y2` (title, format). Independent scale for rates, percents, or a second unit.

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: phase-3 extras, `interact`, or Mermaid. A lone bar or line is cheaper as `charts/bar` / `charts/line`; use combo when marks or axes actually differ.
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { combo } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/combo"; export const render = createRenderer([combo]); // Combo mounts axes + range-band helpers with the renderer. // No separate measured-sizes “combo” row — prefer core/all in hosts (64,372 B gzip).`

label: Gauge
title: Gauge
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. A single value on an arc from `@chartkitdev/core`. Put the number in `metric` (not top-level `data`) — value, min, max, optional target and colored bands.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. A single value on an arc from `@chartkitdev/core`. Put the number in `metric` (not top-level `data`) — value, min, max, optio
anatomy: 1Arc scale — from `metric.min` to `metric.max` (defaults 0–100). Shape the sweep with `mark.startAngle` / `mark.endAngle` and thickness with `mark.strokeWidth`.
2Value — `metric.value` fills the arc (and drives the center readout). Format via `metric.format`.
3Target & bands — `metric.target` marks a goal; `metric.bands[]` paint good/warn/bad ranges (`from`, `to`, `color`, `label`).

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: `interact`, phase-3 extras, or a linear bar gauge (use `bullet`). Do not put `value` at the top level of the spec — validators expect it under `metric`.
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { gauge } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/gauge"; export const render = createRenderer([gauge]); // No separate measured-sizes “gauge” row — prefer core/all in hosts (64,372 B gzip). // progress-ring / kpi reuse $defs/metric with different renderers.`

label: Heatmap
title: Heatmap
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Color-encoded cells from `@chartkitdev/core`. Required channels are `encoding.x` and `encoding.color`. Add `encoding.y` (or `mark.layout: "grid"`) for a matrix; omit `y` or set `mark.layout: "calendar"` for a week×weekday calendar.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Color-encoded cells from `@chartkitdev/core`. Required channels are `encoding.x` and `encoding.color`. Add `encoding.y` (or `

options.role: Row category; implies grid when layout omitted

anatomy: 1Layout — `mark.layout: "calendar"` (date `x`, weeks×weekdays; `mark.weeks` caps columns) or `"grid"` / implied grid when `encoding.y` is set (x×y categories).
2Color channel — required `encoding.color` (the cell value). Optional `scale.scheme`: blue · teal · orange · violet; or `range` / sequential · diverging · quantize · threshold.
3Cell chrome — `mark.gap` (0–1 band fraction) and `mark.cornerRadius`. Calendar cells stay square-ish (cap 32px); unsized calendars stay at 12px.

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: putting the value on `encoding.y` (that is the row for grid). Color lives on `encoding.color`. Sampling (`mark.sampling`) is ignored for heatmap (CK3010).
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { heatmap } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/heatmap"; export const render = createRenderer([heatmap]); // No separate measured-sizes “heatmap” row — prefer core/all in hosts (64,372 B gzip). // encoding.x + encoding.color required; y or mark.layout selects grid vs calendar.`

label: Candlestick
title: Candle
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. OHLC bodies and wicks from `@chartkitdev/core`. Schema type is `candlestick`. Required channels: `encoding.x`, `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`. Optional `encoding.volume` draws a volume pane under the price plot.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. OHLC bodies and wicks from `@chartkitdev/core`. Schema type is `candlestick`. Required channels: `encoding.x`, `open`, `high`

options.role: Time or category for each candle
svg · canvas · auto (canvas OK for candles)

anatomy: 1OHLC candle — body from open→close; wick from high→low. Up uses theme `positive`, down uses `negative`. Channels: `encoding.open` / `high` / `low` / `close`.
2Volume pane — when `encoding.volume` is set, a ~20% height bar strip under the price plot (same up/down colors at lower opacity).
3Gap & zoom — `mark.gap` (default 0.3) sets body width in the band. Wheel/pinch zoom defaults to `interaction.zoom: "x"` for candlestick (elsewhere default `none`).

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: putting OHLC on `encoding.y`. Use the dedicated `open`/`high`/`low`/`close` channels. Volume is optional; omit it to hide the under-pane.
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { candlestick } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/candlestick"; export const render = createRenderer([candlestick]); // No separate measured-sizes “candlestick” row — prefer core/all (64,372 B gzip). // type string is candlestick; docs nav label is Candle.`

label: Scatter
title: Scatter
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Points by two quantitative fields from `@chartkitdev/core`. Optional `encoding.size` makes bubbles; optional `encoding.color` splits categories. Log scales on `x`/`y` are common when values span orders of magnitude.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Points by two quantitative fields from `@chartkitdev/core`. Optional `encoding.size` makes bubbles; optional `encoding.color`

options.role: Default radius when size channel omitted

anatomy: 1Position — quantitative `encoding.x` and `encoding.y` (required). Set `scale.type` to `log`, `linear`, `sqrt`, etc. when the domain needs it.
2Size (bubble) — optional `encoding.size` with `field` and `range` `[minPx, maxPx]`. Scatter-only size channel in the schema.
3Color — optional `encoding.color` (category field or constant). Marker shape/radius also via `mark.pointShape` / `mark.pointSize`; `mark.opacity` applies to scatter.

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: treating size as a second y. Bubble size is `encoding.size` only. Chart-size width/height stays under top-level `size` (not the encoding channel).
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { scatter } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/scatter"; export const render = createRenderer([scatter]); // No separate measured-sizes “scatter” row — prefer core/all (64,372 B gzip). // encoding.size is the bubble channel; omit it for fixed mark.pointSize dots.`

label: KPI
title: Kpi
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Metric card from `@chartkitdev/core`: `metric.label`, `metric.value`, `metric.delta`, optional sparkline from a plain `data` number array. Put value/delta under `metric`, not at the top level.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Metric card from `@chartkitdev/core`: `metric.label`, `metric.value`, `metric.delta`, optional sparkline from a plain `data`

options.role: Change vs prior period (fraction by default)
up · down — which delta direction is good

anatomy: 1Metric — `metric.label` + required `metric.value`. Format with `metric.format` (`compact`, `number`, `currency`, …).
2Delta — `metric.delta` as a fraction (0.125 = +12.5%) unless `deltaFormat` says otherwise. `goodDirection` `up`|`down` sets positive/negative color.
3Sparkline — optional plain number array in `data`. Sampling ignored on kpi (CK3010).

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: top-level `value`/`delta` (use `metric`). Encoding x/y are unused — for a standalone sparkline chart use `type: "sparkline"`.
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { kpi } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/kpi"; export const render = createRenderer([kpi]); // No separate measured-sizes “kpi” row — prefer core/all (64,372 B gzip). // Put value/delta under metric; optional data: number[] draws the sparkline.`

label: Sparkline
title: Sparkline
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Tiny axis-less trend line from `@chartkitdev/core`. `data` may be a plain number array (field name is `value`, x is the index). Default height is 32px — built for inline use beside a KPI or label.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Tiny axis-less trend line from `@chartkitdev/core`. `data` may be a plain number array (field name is `value`, x is the index
anatomy: 1Data — plain `number[]` (sparkline, mini-area, spike). Field is `value`; x is the index. Row objects with encoding also work.
2Stroke — `mark.strokeWidth`, `mark.curve` (`monotone` default; smooth/spline/basis repair to monotone), optional `mark.glow`.
3Fill — `mark.fill` under the line; `mark.gradient` fades toward the baseline. Prefer `type: "mini-area"` when fill is the point.

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: axes, legends, or a metric card chrome — embed the SVG inline. For label + value + delta + spark, use `type: "kpi"` with `data`.
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { sparkline } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/sparkline"; export const render = createRenderer([sparkline]); // No separate measured-sizes “sparkline” row — prefer core/all (64,372 B gzip). // Default height 32px. For a filled inline chart use type: "mini-area".`

label: Mini area
title: Mini-area
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Tiny axis-less filled area from `@chartkitdev/core`. Like sparkline, `data` may be a plain number array — but the fill is the point. Use when the trend band matters more than a single stroke.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Tiny axis-less filled area from `@chartkitdev/core`. Like sparkline, `data` may be a plain number array — but the fill is the
anatomy: 1Data — plain `number[]` (sparkline, mini-area, spike). Field is `value`; x is the index.
2Fill — always drawn for mini-area. `mark.gradient` fades toward the baseline; `mark.fillOpacity` tunes strength.
3Stroke / curve — `mark.strokeWidth` on the top edge; `mark.curve` (`monotone` default). Sampling via `mark.sample`.

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: stacked layers or axes — that is `stacked-area` / `line`. Mini-area is a single series band for inline chrome.
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { miniArea } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/mini-area"; export const render = createRenderer([miniArea]); // No separate measured-sizes “mini-area” row — prefer core/all (64,372 B gzip). // type must be "mini-area". For stroke-only inline use type: "sparkline".`

label: Progress ring
title: Progress-ring
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Circular progress for a single value between `metric.min` and `metric.max` from `@chartkitdev/core`. Put value/min/max under `metric`, not at the top level — same pattern as gauge and kpi.
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Circular progress for a single value between `metric.min` and `metric.max` from `@chartkitdev/core`. Put value/min/max under
anatomy: 1Metric — required `metric.value`; scale via `metric.min` (default 0) and `metric.max` (default 100). Optional `label` and `format`.
2Arc — `mark.strokeWidth` sets arc width; `mark.startAngle` / `endAngle` (degrees; 0 = top of … gauge/donut convention — progress-ring uses degrees, clockwise). `mark.cornerRadius` / end style apply.
3Track — background ring under the progress arc (mock chip; production uses theme track tokens).

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: gauge bands/target needle, or donut category slices. Progress-ring is one value on a circular scale.
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { progressRing } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/progress-ring"; export const render = createRenderer([progressRing]); // No separate measured-sizes “progress-ring” row — prefer core/all (64,372 B gzip). // Put value/min/max under metric. For a semicircle with bands use type: "gauge".`

label: Spike
title: Spike
lede: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Event/spike chart from `@chartkitdev/core`: thin vertical spikes from a baseline over time. Last of the schema Core 14 — plain `number[]` data also works (field `value`, x = index).
description: A JSON spec any agent can emit — beautiful by default. Event/spike chart from `@chartkitdev/core`: thin vertical spikes from a baseline over time. Last of the schema Core 14 — plai
anatomy: 1Series — `encoding.x` (time/category) + `encoding.y` (magnitude), or plain `number[]`.
2Baseline — `mark.baseline` (spike-only). Values rise from this level; zeros sit on the baseline.
3Stem — `mark.strokeWidth`, `mark.opacity` (scatter + spike). Sampling via `mark.sample`.

notes.title: Import
paragraphs: Does not include: bar width or stacking. Spikes are stems from a baseline — good for event/intensity series over time.
code: `import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { spike } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/spike"; export const render = createRenderer([spike]); // No separate measured-sizes “spike” row — prefer core/all (64,372 B gzip). // mark.baseline is spike-only. For thick category bars use type: "bar".`
